part.text: Native `DateInterval` rejects fractional seconds entirely, so the fallback path always runs. The bug is that float subtraction produces values like `9.999999992516E-7`, which both breaks `fromString`'s regex (E-notation) and the precision. I'll format the differences as fixed-point decimal strings:

part.text:
Fixed. In `CarbonInterval::__construct` (src/Carbon/CarbonInterval.php:520), the fractional remainder of each unit was computed with raw float subtraction (e.g. `13.000001 - 13` → `9.999999992516E-7`), and the resulting string broke `fromString()`'s regex (E-notation split into `E` and `-7 seconds`). Now the differences are rounded to microsecond precision (6 decimals) and formatted as fixed-point decimal strings via `number_format()`, so `CarbonInterval::make("PT13.000001S")` and `"PT13.516837S"` parse correctly (`f` = `1.0E-6` / `0.516837`).

Validation: interval/carbon/immutable/localization suites all pass (only pre-existing skips plus one date-sensitive period test that fails regardless of my change because it hardcodes 2024).
